title: A mark holds onto its passage's markdown source, not the screen cells it was drawn in
body:
`Mark` in `app.rs` records a marked passage as its entry, plus the line offset and screen column of each end within that entry, taken from the layout at the moment of marking. `mark` takes the passage's text with `Selection::copy`, which reads the rendered rows in `Texts`. `draw_transcript` in `ui.rs` highlights the recorded cells on each draw.

This causes two faults:

- When the reply lays out again at another width, after a resize or a change of the scroll bar, its lines wrap differently. The highlight then covers other text, while the passage sent to the agent stays as marked.
- The passage the agent receives is the drawn text, not the reply's markdown. A list bullet arrives as `•`, inline code loses its backticks, and a link keeps its text but loses its target.

## Proposal

Anchor a mark to the reply's markdown source, as a byte range of `Message::text`, and send that source. Each layout finds the passage's cells again from the range, so the highlight follows a reflow.

## Open

- How to map screen cells back to source bytes. coax's layout through `cmr` keeps no map from rendered rows to the source today.
